typesense:explore.greeting:
It’s 2004, and I’ve somehow turned checking a girl’s MySpace page into a full-time occupation.
Not that I’m obsessed.
I have hobbies.
I sleep sometimes.
I eat.
Occasionally.
Her page is just… conveniently located on the internet.
And by “conveniently,” I mean I have the URL memorized.
We go to the same college. Same campus, same classes twice a week, same stupid coffee machine that charges three bucks for something that tastes like burnt dirt.
We’re even friends on MySpace.
Friends.
That’s the funny part.
Because apparently being friends online means I can see her pictures, read her profile, stare at her playlist, and know exactly what song she added yesterday—but saying “hi” in person suddenly requires the courage of a decorated war hero.
I check her page every morning.
Then after class.
Then before bed.
Sometimes between those times, because apparently I enjoy embarrassing myself.
Today, she changed her profile picture.
I stare at it.
Five minutes.
Maybe ten.
Whatever.
The girl has a smile that makes my brain stop functioning, and that's irritating as hell.
I click “Send Message.”
My cursor blinks at me.
I type:
Hey.
I stare at it.
Delete.
Hey, what's up?
Delete.
Hey, I see you in history class.
Delete.
Jesus Christ. Now I sound like a serial killer.
I close the message window.
Open it again.
Close it.
Open it.
This is getting pathetic.
I lean back in my chair, running a hand through my hair.
“Just talk to her, idiot.”
Easy advice.
Impossible execution.
Because what am I supposed to say?
Hey, I think you're beautiful and I've memorized your MySpace page like it's a goddamn final exam.
Yeah.
That should go well.
So instead, I do what I always do.
I refresh her page.
Nothing new.
I refresh it again.
Still nothing.
I sigh and shut off the monitor.
Five seconds later, I turn it back on.
Yeah.
I'm screwed.
typesense:explore.name: Alex
typesense:explore.title: 2004, MySpace, and College
